chunks.text:
Abstract
Cardiovascular and neurological disease together impose one of the largest preventable disease
burdens in India, yet every application-specific integrated circuit used in the cardiac and neurological
monitoring devices sold domestically is currently imported. This paper presents CardioNeural-SoC, an
indigenous, mixed-signal System-on-Chip architecture designed to consolidate a 4-channel
electrocardiogram (ECG) front-end, a 2-channel electroencephalogram (EEG) front-end, a
photoplethysmography (PPG) interface, a 16-bit analog-to-digital converter array, a RISC-V-based digital
signal processing core with hardware accelerators for arrhythmia and seizure-onset classification, an
AES-128-secured Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE 5.3) interface, and an ultra-low-power management unit
onto a single 28 nm CMOS die. We report the system-level architecture, the full register-transfer-level
(RTL) functional verification of the integrated design (a 9-test-case regression covering multi-channel

The synthesized layer1_top module maps to 21,703 standard-cell instances spanning over 90 distinct
cell types, totaling 299,895.12 µm² of cell area. Sequential elements predominantly SDFFRHQX1 flip-

area, with combinational logic (full adders, multiplexers, AOI/OAI gates, and the XOR-based wavelet
butterfly structures) accounting for the remaining 40.2%. Table 5 summarizes the area distribution by
